cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Rotation of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) so the inside shoulder turns away from the defender's side, reducing the frontal width of the torso. Measured as the image-plane shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading - a larger rotation means a narrower profile presented. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender - getting skinny - so the receiver presents the narrowest possible surface as he clears the contact window.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Running through the release square-shouldered, presenting a full chest for the defender to get hands on and re-route the receiver.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) relative to the hip line and to the stance's facing direction. Measurable from a static frame; whether the rotation matches the INTENDED release direction needs the release itself or a declared route.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Standard - Stance - Shoulder Alignment
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Square and quiet - don't tip the release.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Shoulders remain controlled and aligned with the intended release position. The upper body should not rotate excessively away from the line before movement begins.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders rotated away from the line before the snap, telegraphing the release direction to the defender, or shoulder line unlevel enough to unbalance the first step.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center reaching zero, plus ankle separation held at its wide breakdown value and positional variance of both ankles across the pause frames. The measurement is a genuine momentary stop on a wide base, not a slow drift through.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The wide, low stance holds for a beat as forward velocity reaches zero - the receiver is genuinely stopped, not still drifting.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Still carrying forward velocity through the pause, so the receiver drifts past the break point and the route depth is wrong; or the base narrowing and losing the platform for the plant.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak velocity and amplitude of wrist displacement on the first strides out of the break, compared against the compact position held through the breakdown and pause - the arms should re-extend into a hard punch-like pump immediately.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The arms fire back into a violent punch-like pump the instant the drive out begins, mechanically restoring sprint momentum from a standing stop.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arms staying compact or pumping weakly out of the break, so the upper body adds nothing to rebuilding speed from a dead stop - where it matters most.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the outside (plant) foot at ground contact - target is zero drift, the foot gripping rather than sliding. Plus the rate at which Pelvis Center velocity along the 45 degree diagonal falls to zero, which measures how completely the forward momentum was arrested. Contact time from strike to toe-off indicates the violence of the brake.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: On the third step the outside foot slams into the turf along the 45 degree line and grips, acting as a violent brake that kills the inside momentum in one contact.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: The plant foot sliding or drifting at contact rather than gripping, so the momentum is not arrested and the receiver needs extra steps to change direction.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the lead knee relative to Pelvis Center on the first strides out of the break, expressed in torso lengths, plus the forward component of that knee's travel along the new heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The lead knee drives immediately up and forward out of the plant, converting the stored energy into instant acceleration on the new line.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the throwing window closes before he can separate.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift (rounding) accumulating BEFORE the break depth is reached. Break depth target 10-12 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Depth is the ONLY thing distinguishing the In from the Dig (12-15 yards) - the kinematics are identical. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Stem & Load
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Run it straight - no banana.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Sprint hard downfield on a strictly straight line for 10-12 yards, pushing the vertical stem through the defender's outside shoulder to force them to protect the deep outside lane. Two steps before break depth, drop the weight violently into the hips and chop the cleats to counteract forward momentum.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Applied to EVERY stride rather than a single plant, unlike the cut techniques. (1) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector at each ground contact - the toe pulled up into a rigid ankle lock. A Foot Index pointing downward at impact is the fault signal. (2) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each strike - landing beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead. (3) LINEARITY: lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, which should stay near zero.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Go - Vertical Run
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toes up every step - don't reach for speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The running stride stays completely natural and uninterrupted, steps landing compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding. The toes pull up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride to hold a rigid, explosive ankle lock against the turf while the eyes track the ball over the shoulder.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to run faster, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability, caps top-end speed, and costs balance down the sideline.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Rate of extension of the hip angle (Shoulder-Hip-Knee vector) at the frame the hands make contact. The measurement is the hip extension firing IN TIME with the hand contact, transferring ground force through the torso into the block.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Hip Drive at Engagement
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips extend hard as the hands make contact, driving ground force up through the torso and into the defender so the block has power behind it rather than just reach.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands landing without hip extension behind them - an arms-only block with no ground force, which the defender sheds easily. Or the hips firing before the hands arrive, wasting the drive.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity at the plant foot's ground contact - target is zero braking velocity along the release heading. Plus lateral distance between the ankles at the plant, which should stay at or below 1.0x shoulder width (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit).
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Plant Step - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The front foot plants firmly with no braking, and the feet stay tight within the body's frame - at or inside shoulder width - so the escape can fire in either direction.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Planting with a braking action that kills momentum, or a base widening beyond shoulder width so the receiver has to gather before escaping.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the outside (plant) foot at ground contact - target is zero drift, the foot gripping rather than sliding. Plus the rate at which the lateral velocity of Pelvis Center falls to zero after the plant, which measures how completely the sideways momentum was arrested. Contact time from strike to toe-off indicates how cleanly the force was delivered.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The outside foot slams aggressively into the turf and grips, arresting all lateral momentum in one contact so it can be converted straight into forward drive.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: SOFT CLEAT PLANT - failing to slam the outside foot into the turf with force. A soft plant results in a slow, sluggish transition from horizontal to vertical, and the foot drifts rather than gripping.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head pitch and yaw from Nose position relative to the ear midpoint - the head should stay level, aimed forward at roughly defender belt/midsection height rather than dipping to the feet or lifting. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model, and the defender is not in frame in a solo clip, so the target line cannot be confirmed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Head / Eyes
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The head stays level and locked forward toward the defender's belt line - reading the hips rather than the hands or the feet.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head dipping toward the feet or lifting off the defender's midsection line during the kickstep. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable, and the defender is not in frame - orientation only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center beginning roughly 2 steps before the break, expressed in torso lengths. Break depth target 10-12 yards - NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Fault signals: wrist displacement amplitude decreasing, or Sternum vertical height RISING, at any point before the break depth is reached. Detailed breakdown mechanics are held in Cuts - Stop.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Stem & Load
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Sell the go - keep pumping, drop your weight late.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards with pads leaning forward and natural full strides, forcing the defender into an aggressive backpedal for fear of the go route. Two steps before break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats to control speed - without standing up or slowing the arm pump.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Sternum, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE DEAD GIVEAWAY - slowing the arm pump or raising the chest before reaching break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the out route. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center - the foot must land strictly under the centre of mass, not ahead of it. Also check the ankle is not ahead of the knee. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - the toe pulled UP pre-impact, with the heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index at touchdown. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a flat 90 degrees toward the sideline relative to the stem heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Out - Power Plant
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toe up, plant under yourself, point it at the sideline.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: As the eyes find the boundary, slam the inside foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes. Instantly pivot and point the toe down a flat 90-degree track toward the sideline, masking the break until the last possible instant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak downward and inward velocity of the trailing wrist and elbow, and whether that path crosses the shoulder line, timed against the breakout push-off. NOTE: the specific hand technique (swipe vs chop) needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path and velocity are measurable from pose.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Breakout - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The trailing arm executes a heavy downward chop past the shoulder line, clearing the defender's arms as the receiver breaks back to the outside.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hand, Right Hand
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: No hand action at the breakout, or an arm path that never crosses the shoulder line, leaving a recovering defender's hands attached through the escape. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak velocity of the trailing wrist and elbow, and whether that path passes above the shoulder plane (swipe / chop / club-rip), timed against the burst stride. NOTE: the specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path, height and velocity are measurable from pose.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The trailing arm drives violently past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or club-rip - shattering the defender's reach as the receiver clears vertically.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hand, Right Hand
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: DROPPING THE HANDS - letting the arms trail behind the body, leaving no protection against a recovering defender's arm bar or jersey pull. Also: an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical elevation of both wrists relative to the shoulder line, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach, wrists clearly above forehead height. Plus elbow flexion angle (slightly flexed, not locked out), and shoulder-midpoint elevation showing the shrug toward the ears. Plus convergence of the THUMBS with index fingers pointing upward, forming the window. NOTE: reliable thumbs-together vs pinkies-together detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER - this distinction is the defining difference between a high and a low catch and the 33-point pose model cannot resolve it reliably.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Center - High - Extend & Bait
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Thumbs together, reach through the roof.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Track the high trajectory and time the jump or extension so the hands intercept the ball at the absolute apex of reach. Shoot both arms violently upward above the forehead with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs pressed tightly together and index fingers pointing up, creating an inverted triangle to look through.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Thumb, Right Thumb, Left Index Finger, Right Index Finger, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: TURNING PINKIES OUT - reaching up for a high ball with the pinkies together instead of the thumbs. This turns the palms away from the ball and makes a clean high catch impossible. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of the wrists and their extension distance from the shoulders along the target vector, at the engagement frame. The measurement is the speed and reach of the punch. NOTE: whether the hands land INSIDE THE DEFENDER'S CHEST FRAME needs the defender in frame; hand placement relative to the receiver's own body is measurable. Grip and finger detail needs the Hand landmarker.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Hand Extension & Shoot Velocity
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands shoot forward violently at engagement, extending fast into the defender's chest frame rather than arriving late or short.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hand, Right Hand, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Slow or short hand extension, so the receiver makes contact with his chest rather than his hands and has no control of the defender. (Hand placement on the defender needs them in frame; grip needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center held at its low breakdown value across the pause frames, expressed in torso lengths - no upward drift while the upper body initiates the turn.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips hold their low position through the pause, staying loaded so the plant can fire without needing to re-sink.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the legs - the receiver then has to drop again before he can drive out, and the break is late.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Front knee flexion angle from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. Reference range 100-120 degrees - acute enough to absorb force and store elastic energy. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule. Which leg is 'front' is resolved from the stance stagger.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Kickstep - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The front knee holds an acute bend - roughly 100 to 120 degrees - absorbing force and storing elastic energy for the escape rather than straightening under the load.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Front knee straightening or losing its bend during the kickstep, so no energy is stored and the escape has to be generated from a standing start.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held across the hesitation frames, compared against their values at the end of the slide - the angles should be maintained and stable, absorbing the lateral force without collapsing or extending.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Both knees stay deep and stable through the pause, absorbing the lateral momentum and holding balance on the wide base.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knees straightening or wobbling during the hesitation, so the receiver loses balance on the wide base or unloads the legs before the transition.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] COMBINED PITCH AND YAW TRACKING at the impact frame - the only catch in the set requiring both simultaneously. The Nose vector must be pitched UPWARD and rotated LATERALLY so it intersects the high-diagonal wrist midpoint. Measured as the angular gap between head direction and wrist midpoint in both axes. The head drifting back toward the body's centre line before the hands close is the fault, and it is detected as yaw returning toward the running heading while the wrists are still out wide. Plus vertical wrist height peaking at or immediately before impact, not after.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Away - High - The Strike
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Stare through the diagonal window - don't drift back to centre.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the base of support (the ankle pair), tracked across the full 5 yards to confirm continuous forward progression rather than only the opening steps.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Weight Transfer Progression
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Weight moves continuously forward across the full 5 yards, staying ahead of the base of support so every step drives rather than catches.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Weight stalling or falling back behind the feet at any point in the 5 yards, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical at the engagement frame, plus absolute shoulder-midpoint height in torso lengths. NOTE: whether the receiver's pads are BELOW THE DEFENDER'S needs the defender in frame - in a solo clip only the receiver's own pad height and torso angle are assessable.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Pad Level at Contact
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: At engagement the shoulders stay low - at or below the defender's pad level - with the torso angled forward so the receiver wins the leverage battle rather than being stood up.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Sternum, Pelvis Center, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Engaging with pads high or the torso upright, letting the defender get underneath and upright the receiver, who then loses the block immediately. (Relative pad level needs the defender in frame.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). Expect a TRANSITION from a wider acceleration base at Steps 1-2 to a narrow, linear running track by Yard 5 - the measurement is the narrowing trend, not any single contact.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Base Width Progression
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The base starts wider through the driving first steps, then narrows progressively into a linear running track by the fifth yard as the receiver transitions from acceleration to running.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Base staying wide through the whole 5 yards, costing efficiency and speed; or narrowing too early so the driving steps lose their power base.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the read frames, expressed in torso lengths - it should hold the low position established at the split with no upward drift.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Hesitation - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips stay low through the read, preserving the loaded position so the receiver can explode in whichever direction the defender opens.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rising during the hesitation, unloading the base - the receiver then has to re-sink before moving, which costs the advantage the split created.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Onset and angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the upfield release lane, timed against the plant's ground contact. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The head begins turning upfield toward the release lane as the plant lands, leading the body into the vertical transition.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head turning well before the plant (telegraphing the vertical) or lagging behind it, so the body commits before the receiver has picked up the lane. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Count and displacement of the vertical acceleration steps along the release heading - target 2 to 3 explosive steps before the break, resolved in the image plane. The fault signal is lateral drift toward the sideline beginning immediately off the line rather than after the vertical steps. Plus a subtle vertical drop of Pelvis Center WITHOUT any reduction in stride length or step frequency - a speed-cut load, not a breakdown. Break depth 1-3 yards. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference; the step COUNT does not, and is the more reliable signal here. Detailed mechanics are held in Cuts - Speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Flat - Stem & Load
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Two hard steps vertical first - don't fade to the sideline.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Explode vertically off the line for 2 to 3 hard steps, driving the pads forward to threaten the defender's leverage and make them respect a vertical release. Then prepare to redirect sideways by subtly sinking the hips, keeping the feet moving at full speed with no choppy or gathering steps.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: FADING EARLY - unconsciously drifting outward toward the sideline right off the snap. This tells the defender exactly where the receiver is going and lets them squeeze him into the boundary. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Linear displacement of Pelvis Center and the ankle path along the stem heading, resolved in the image plane - the fault signal is lateral drift (rounding) accumulating BEFORE the break depth is reached. Break depth target 12-15 yards, requiring a 3-step breakdown rather than the In's 2. NOTE: absolute depth needs a scale reference (player height) and the route to be declared; without them, report the measured depth without judging it. Depth is the ONLY thing distinguishing the Dig from the In (10-12 yards) - the kinematics are identical. NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Stem & Load
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Run it straight and deep - no banana.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Run an ultra-aggressive vertical stem for 12-15 yards, pushing directly at the defender's midsection to freeze their leverage and force a deep backpedal respecting the post or go. At break depth, violently drop the weight into the hips and chop the cleats heavily through a 3-step breakdown to absorb the extra momentum the longer stem has built.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating toward the chosen release direction, timed against the plant foot's ground contact. The rotation should fire WITH the plant, not after it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips turn and open violently toward the chosen lane the instant the plant foot hits, converting the loaded base into directional drive.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips opening slowly or lagging behind the plant, so the drive has no rotational force behind it and the receiver pushes sideways instead of exploding through the lane.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors, held across the slide. Reference range 120-140 degrees. Cross-check vertical variance of Pelvis Center - upward spikes indicate hopping rather than gliding. NOTE: the 120-140 range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Both knees hold a consistent bend - roughly 120 to 140 degrees - through the slide, producing a smooth lateral glide with no upward bounce.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knees extending during the slide, which pops the body upward into a hop; or collapsing so deep the receiver cannot cover ground laterally.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the plant foot's Foot Index at ground contact - the shoulders should sit over or slightly ahead of the planting toe. Shoulders falling behind the plant foot is the fault signal and correlates with backward slippage.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The torso leans securely out over the planting toe, keeping the weight stacked over the anchor so the receiver does not slip backward off the plant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders sitting back behind the plant foot, so the weight is behind the anchor and the receiver slips backward instead of driving out.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum, and the speed of their rise into position during the split. Wrists should reach chest / lower-Sternum height. Elbow flexion angle for a tight, compact ready position rather than extended arms.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands come up quickly to chest height into a tight, relaxed ready position as the feet land - loaded to strike but not tense.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands staying low or arriving late, so the receiver has nothing ready when the defender's hands come. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Torso drive angle of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector relative to vertical, held low and forward across the push step. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to confirm a whole-body sprint posture rather than folding at the waist.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The torso stays low and forward in an aggressive sprinting posture through the push step, matching what a genuine slant would look like.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Torso rising toward upright during the push step, which tips that a plant is coming rather than a continued sprint inside.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the torso vector (hip midpoint to shoulder midpoint) relative to vertical across the acceleration phase. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to distinguish a whole-body lean from waist flexion.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Body Lean
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The torso leans forward through the initial acceleration, driving the body out of the stance. The lean comes from the whole body angled forward, not from bending at the waist.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Spine, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Standing straight up out of the stance, killing acceleration; or bending at the waist so the chest folds forward ahead of the hips instead of the whole body leaning.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Lateral extension distance of both wrists away from Sternum, resolved in the image plane perpendicular to the running heading, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach to the catch side. Plus BOTH wrists extending together (a single extended wrist is the one-hand fault). Plus partial shoulder-line rotation toward the catch side WITHOUT the hip line following - the lower body must hold its running line. Plus thumb and index convergence forming the diamond. NOTE: hand shape needs the HAND LANDMARKER; extension, torque and stride continuity are measurable today.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Away - Chest/Mid - Extend & Bait
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Two hands out wide - turn your chest, not your feet.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Thumb, Right Thumb, Left Index Finger, Right Index Finger, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. Also: the hips rotating with the chest, which breaks the running line and costs stride. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Final angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) relative to the upfield heading once the escape is complete - target is fully rotated onto the vertical track. Plus the time taken from the plant to reach that alignment.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips rotate fully to point straight downfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track so the route can develop at full speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips never finishing their rotation, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically, which costs separation and distorts the route.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the foot must land directly under the hips, not out in front of the chest frame. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector, with the Heel reaching its lowest vertical position BEFORE the Foot Index at touchdown. A toe-first, downward-pointing strike is the fault signal. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pointing directly back down the stem line - a full 180 degree reversal toward the line of scrimmage.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Power Plant
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toe up, under your hips - point it back at the line.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: As the eyes find the quarterback, drive the cutting foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the hips. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes instantly. Pivot and direct the toe back down the stem toward the line of scrimmage, holding the illusion of a forward sprint until the exact moment of the cut.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE LUNGING TOE PLANT - reaching too far forward with the planting step and letting the toe point downward before contact. This strips core stability, causes a slide, and tips off the defender early because the running stride visibly changes before the cut.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the swinging knee relative to Pelvis Center on each stride, expressed in torso lengths, sustained at top-speed values through the stem.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The knees drive at full sprint height through the stem, generating the maximum speed that the breakdown will then have to absorb.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knee drive dropping off during the stem, slowing the receiver early and removing the vertical threat the stop cut depends on.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Lead knee flexion angle plus the lateral direction of the knee's travel, measured from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. The knee should drive inward across the body, pointing along the inside fake path rather than staying square or collapsing.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The lead knee flexes and drives aggressively inward across the body, pointing along the inside fake path to sell the release direction.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Lead knee staying square or trailing the foot across, so the lower body does not commit and the fake reads as a feint rather than a release.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center across the breakdown steps, expressed in torso lengths - a drastic sink relative to its stem height. Pelvis Center remaining high on entry to the breakdown is the fault signal, and correlates with insufficient knee flexion.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips drop drastically on the breakdown steps, dumping the centre of gravity low so the legs can absorb the speed and the body can anchor.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: STIFF LEG - entering the breakdown with the hips still high, so the deceleration is absorbed through the knees rather than the whole lower body. Slower to stop and hard on the joints.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact through the approach, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) - should remain at or above 1.0x, significantly wider than a normal running stride. NOTE: the 1.0x figure is an uncalibrated starting reference.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Wide Base Preservation
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The base stays wide throughout the approach - noticeably wider than a running stride - so the receiver keeps blocking leverage and can react laterally to the defender.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Base narrowing into a normal running stride as the receiver closes, so he arrives with no lateral leverage and gets moved off the block on contact.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of the shoulder midpoint expressed in torso lengths, and its rate of rise across the first three steps. Gradual rise is correct; a step-change (spiking upright) is the fault.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Pad Level
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise gradually across the first steps as speed builds, rather than popping upright immediately.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders spiking upright on the first step rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and slowing acceleration.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating toward the new break direction, compared against head yaw velocity across the same frames - the shoulders should FOLLOW the head, not lead it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The shoulders rotate in behind the head turn, shifting the body's equilibrium toward the new break so the plant can redirect immediately.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders rotating before or without the head, so the body commits blind and the receiver is late picking up the ball out of the break.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the planting leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector at ground contact. Reference range 90-110 degrees - acute enough to absorb the lateral kinetic energy and convert it into straight-line power. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The planting knee bends sharply - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - absorbing the lateral energy of the slide and converting it into straight-line power.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the lateral force - the receiver slides through the plant or has to take a recovery step before going vertical.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak lateral velocity of the wrists toward the inside lane, resolved in the image plane, timed against the crossover step. The arm pump should fire with the foot and hips, not after them.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Crossover - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The arms pump hard toward the inside lane in time with the crossover step, mimicking a genuine release so the fake is complete from feet to hands.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arms staying passive during the crossover, or pumping late so the upper body lags the feet and the fake looks manufactured. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Both ankles leaving the ground within the same frame window (simultaneous lift), then rear ankle displacing forward and front ankle slightly back along the release heading, landing parallel. Final ankle separation greater than 1.0x shoulder width (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). NOTE: fore-aft displacement resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Split - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Both feet leave the ground at the same instant, the back foot snapping forward and the front foot back, landing parallel and wider than shoulder width to establish a balanced, uncommitted base.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: OVER-SPLITTING - landing far too wide, which locks up the hips so the receiver cannot push off to change direction. Also: feet leaving the ground at different times rather than together, or landing staggered instead of parallel.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] DIAGONAL extension of both wrists - combining vertical elevation above the shoulder line AND lateral displacement away from Sternum, resolved in the image plane, expressed in torso lengths. The measurement is the resultant diagonal reach, target roughly 45 degrees up and out. Plus elbow flexion (slightly flexed, not locked), shoulder-midpoint elevation showing the shrug up and out, and THUMB convergence with index fingers pointing diagonally up. NOTE: thumbs-together vs pinkies-up detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Away - High - Extend & Bait
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Up and out at 45 - thumbs locked.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Thumb, Right Thumb, Left Index Finger, Right Index Finger, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the shoulder line (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating toward the break, compared against the head's yaw velocity across the same frames - the two should track together. Plus shoulder-line tilt, which creates the deceptive body lean.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The shoulders turn in time with the head, tilting into the new direction so the upper body initiates the cut and blindsides the defender before the feet move.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders lagging behind the head turn or staying square, so the upper body does not lead the cut and the transition has to be driven entirely by the plant.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center displacement vector across the approach - it should track a consistent line toward the target rather than drifting. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so alignment to THEIR position cannot be measured; only the consistency and straightness of the receiver's own approach path is assessable.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Lateral Alignment / Tracking
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The receiver tracks a consistent line onto the defender, staying square to them so they cannot slip past inside or outside before the hands fit.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Nose, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Drifting off the tracking line during the approach, so the defender slips past inside or outside before contact is made. (Alignment to the defender needs them in frame - path consistency only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center sustained after the contact frame, together with base width and knee flexion held at their engagement values. The measurement is all three continuing together - drive without losing the base or standing up.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Post-Contact Cleat Drive
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The feet keep driving after contact, moving the defender while the base stays wide and the knees stay bent - the block is sustained rather than a single hit.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Stopping the feet on contact and leaning on the defender, or standing up and narrowing the base after the hit - either way the block is lost within a second.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Knee angle from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors on both legs; plus horizontal tracking of the front knee over the front Foot Index (knee-over-toe). Measurable from a static frame.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Standard - Stance - Knee Flexion
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Knee over toe - bent and loaded, never locked.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Front knee is bent rather than locked. The knee tracks forward toward the toe while maintaining an athletic loaded position. Rear knee remains flexed enough to contribute to the first movement.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Front knee locked or straight, knee collapsing inside or outside the toe line, or rear knee too extended to contribute to the first movement.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the foot must land directly under the hips, not out in front of the chest frame. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector, with the Heel reaching its lowest vertical position BEFORE the Foot Index at touchdown.
