cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The shoulders stay completely square to the stem and forward over the knees during the load - the upper body reveals nothing while the lower body prepares.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Left Knee, Right Knee
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders starting to rotate toward the break during the load step, an early tell that lets the defender jump the route.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of the inside shoulder relative to the outside shoulder (shoulder-line tilt angle) at the plant, plus the resulting reduction in the torso's frontal profile. A pronounced dip lowers the chest profile against the defender's leverage.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The inside shoulder dips at the plant, lowering the chest profile and getting skinny against the defender's leverage as the transition begins.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Staying square and upright through the plant, presenting a full chest just as the receiver commits and giving the defender a clean target to re-route.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement front-to-back through the stem, held at full sprint values. Cross-check contralateral timing against the legs.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The arms pump violently through the stem at full sprint amplitude, driving the vertical push and giving no hint the break is coming.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arm pump shortening or slowing during the stem, a visual tell that the receiver is about to break down.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each touchdown. Landing under or slightly behind Pelvis Center during the early steps prevents negative horizontal (braking) velocity at strike. Cross-check ankle horizontal velocity at strike - negative relative to the heading is braking.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Foot Strike / Braking Elimination
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Each foot lands under or slightly behind the hips during the acceleration steps, so every strike drives the body forward instead of braking it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Pelvis Center, Left Knee, Right Knee
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Foot landing ahead of the hips at strike, creating a braking force that costs speed on every step - typically caused by overstriding out of the stance.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center on the load step, expressed in torso lengths - a small controlled drop (roughly an inch on an adult frame). Critically, cross-check forward velocity across the same window: it must NOT decrease. An upward spike in Pelvis Center or Sternum height is the fault signal.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Load - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips drop a small, controlled amount to load the cut - without losing any forward speed. The sink is subtle enough that the defender cannot see it coming.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: POPPING UP - a sudden upward spike in hip or chest height, destroying the low sprint angle and broadcasting the break. Also: sinking so far that forward velocity drops and the cut becomes a gather.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of both wrists relative to Sternum held elevated across the pause, plus distance from each wrist to Sternum staying compact. Active hands show as small continuous motion rather than being frozen or dropped.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands stay elevated and active in a compact frame through the pause, ready to catch and tight enough not to slow the rotation.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands dropping or going wide during the pause, so the receiver is neither ready for a quick throw nor compact enough to turn fast. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Positional variance of Pelvis Center and the shoulder midpoint across the pre-snap frames - low variance indicates a settled stance, excessive variance indicates swaying or rocking. Requires a sequence of frames rather than a single static frame, so it needs the dynamic pipeline.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Standard - Stance - Stance Stability / Readiness
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Still but not stiff - loaded and ready to go.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Receiver remains stable but immediately movable. The stance is sufficiently loaded to prevent a false step while allowing explosive movement in the intended release direction.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Swaying, rocking, or bouncing pre-snap rather than settling into a loaded position; or so rigid and locked that the first movement requires a reset. A false step at the snap is the downstream symptom.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak upward velocity of the wrists as the plant lands, and whether the hands reach a strike-ready height relative to Sternum. The hand action should fire with the plant, not after it. NOTE: the specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker; arm path and timing are measurable from pose.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The React and Plant - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands come up fast into an aggressive strike position as the plant lands, ready to meet the defender if they reach out at the transition.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands staying passive or low through the plant, leaving the receiver defenceless at the exact moment the defender is most likely to reach. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the swinging knee relative to Pelvis Center on each stride, expressed in torso lengths. Should hold at top-speed values through the stem rather than dropping off.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Preparation - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The front knee lifts high through the swing phase on every stride, sustaining genuine top-end speed down the stem.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knee lift dropping off during the stem, which slows the receiver and signals that he is preparing to break rather than running deep.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical rise of the front heel relative to its own Foot Index (heel lifting while the toe stays down), timed against the onset of forward Pelvis Center velocity. Correct order is heel lift LEADING forward travel.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Front-Foot Roll-Off
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the drive - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak forward acceleration of Pelvis Center along the release heading immediately after the plant's toe-off, resolved in the image plane, plus the contact time of that push-off. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z. The defender's hip plane is not in frame in a solo clip, so clearance is inferred from the path rather than confirmed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The plant foot drives explosively forward, accelerating the receiver past the defender's hip plane and clearing their level in one burst rather than easing into the route.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: A slow or gradual push-off out of the plant, so the receiver never clears the defender's level and stays inside their reach as the route develops. (Defender position is not in frame - path and acceleration only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Displacement of the escape step along the release heading, resolved in the image plane, plus the lateral offset of the Pelvis Center path - the track should be tight and angled past the defender's hip rather than wide or into them. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the heading, not via MediaPipe Z. The defender's hip plane is not in frame in a solo clip, so clearance is inferred from path tightness rather than confirmed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Vertical Escape - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The escape step drives straight upfield on a tight angled path past the defender's hip, clearing their level entirely rather than drifting wide or running into them.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: SLAMMING INTO THE DB - releasing directly into the defender's body instead of taking an angled, tight path past their hip. The aim is to clear their frame, not initiate a collision. Also: drifting wide of the track and losing ground. (Defender position is not in frame - path tightness only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the hesitation frames, expressed in torso lengths - it should hold low with no upward drift, preserving the compressed-spring position.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips stay low and loaded through the hesitation, holding the compressed position so the forward transition can fire without a reset.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rising during the pause, unloading the spring - the receiver then has to sink again before transitioning, which gives the defender time to recover.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal ankle velocity of the plant foot at ground contact - target is zero slide. Plus the plant foot's position relative to Pelvis Center: it plants on the OPPOSITE side to the intended release, so the push drives the body into the chosen lane. Contact time from strike to toe-off measures how cleanly the force was delivered.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The foot opposite the intended path slams cleanly into the turf with no slide, delivering full force to drive the body laterally and forward into the open lane.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: CLICK-BACK - dragging the driving foot instead of slamming it cleanly into the turf, which bleeds away the explosive power. Also: the foot sliding at contact rather than gripping.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle between the shoulder line and the hip line (rotational separation) - target is zero. Plus shoulder-line angle relative to the release heading, which should stay square, and shoulder-line tilt, which should stay level. NOTE: squareness resolved as the image-plane shoulder-line angle, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Lateral Slide - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The shoulders stay wide, level and square to the defender, moving with the hips rather than rotating independently of them.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders rotating away from the hips during the slide, disconnecting the upper body and signalling the release direction before the receiver has committed.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Time between crossover foot ground contact and toe-off (contact time - shorter is better), plus peak acceleration of Pelvis Center toward the outside vertical lane immediately after, resolved in the image plane. The measurement is the instantaneous redirect, not the top speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The crossover foot plants and immediately pushes off into the outside lane - no gather step, no pause. The redirect is instantaneous, converting the fake straight into the escape.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: A gather step or hesitation between the crossover and the burst, giving the defender time to recover and closing the outside lane the fake just opened.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Displacement of Pelvis Center after the plant, resolved along the 45-degree downhill vector in the image plane - the fault signal is near-zero displacement (standing still) after the break. Plus the shoulder line squaring to the new heading, and horizontal distance of both wrists from Sternum increasing at the catch point (hands extended away from the frame). NOTE: whether the receiver actually shortened the throw or shielded a defender needs the ball and the defender in frame.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Comeback - Finish
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Come back to the ball - never wait on it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot and work back downhill toward the ball, shortening the distance of the throw, squaring the shoulders to the quarterback to shield the ball, and securing the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: WAITING ON THE BALL - standing still after making the cut. The receiver must actively run back downhill toward the ball to stop a trailing defender undercutting the route for an interception. (Ball position and defender leverage are not pose-measurable.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector relative to vertical, transitioning from the stem's forward sprint lean to a more upright tucked position. Plus horizontal position of the shoulder midpoint relative to the knees - the shoulders should come back inside the knee frame rather than staying out over the toes.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The forward sprint lean shifts back into a tucked, balanced position with the shoulders inside the knee frame, so the receiver can anchor rather than being carried forward.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Left Knee, Right Knee, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders staying out over the toes through the breakdown, so momentum carries the chest forward and the receiver cannot stop cleanly or has to take recovery steps.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating toward the middle of the field, and the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead. Plus shoulder-line rotation following the head. NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually READ the inside linebackers is not confirmable from pose.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Visual Snap
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Snap the eyes inside - see the window before you turn.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: At the absolute peak of deceleration, snap the head and eyes around to face the middle of the field first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the inside linebackers before the body commits.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks into the middle without having cleared his vision for crashing inside defenders. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Spine vector (Pelvis Center to Sternum) relative to vertical, held at an acute forward sprint lean through the stem. Cross-check against the hip-to-knee vector to confirm whole-body lean rather than waist flexion.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Preparation - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The torso holds an aggressive forward sprint lean through the stem, the posture of a receiver running past the defender rather than one preparing to stop.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Torso rising toward upright during the stem, an early tell that the receiver is preparing to break down.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angular change of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) from its lateral orientation during the slide to alignment with the upfield heading - approximately a 90 degree flip. Plus the angular velocity of that rotation and the time taken to complete it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips flip sharply from the lateral slide orientation to point straight upfield, locking the receiver onto the vertical track in a single decisive rotation.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rotating slowly or only partway, leaving the receiver running at an angle across the field rather than vertically - the slide's advantage is lost in the transition.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a flat 90 degrees, aligned immediately after the plant rather than settling over several strides. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory continuing DOWNFIELD rather than staying flat across. Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Dig - Finish
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Flat across - don't drift downfield.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat across the field, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: RUNNING FLAT / BANANING - letting the route drift downfield toward the defensive backfield instead of holding a flat, razor-sharp 90-degree line across the middle.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement front-to-back at lower-Sternum height, plus contralateral timing against the legs. The pattern should match a genuine sprint start, not a token arm movement.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The arms pump hard at chest height in a genuine sprint-start rhythm, matching what a real slant release would look like.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Passive or low-amplitude arm action that does not match a real sprint, leaving the upper body out of step with the feet and weakening the fake.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Elbow flexion angle from the Shoulder-Elbow-Wrist vectors, plus contralateral timing: opposite arm and leg reaching peak forward extension within the same frame window. Also check wrist horizontal position relative to Sternum - crossing the body's midline indicates transverse swing.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Arm Drive & Contralateral Timing
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Arms drive front-to-back in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - at a consistent elbow angle, without swinging across the body.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Hand, Right Hand, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arms out of sync with the legs, swinging across the body's midline rather than driving front-to-back, or elbows flailing and locking so the arms add no drive.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held locked on the 45 degree inside path across the push step, measured as low angular variance. Any rotation toward the outside before the plant is a tell. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Push Step - Head / Eyes
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The head stays locked straight down the inside path through the push step, holding the deception right up until the plant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head turning back toward the outside before the plant, breaking the deception early and letting the defender sit on the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Lateral distance between the ankles at each ground contact, expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit) so it stays size-independent.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 1 Step - Base Width
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Feet stay under the body through the first steps - narrow enough to run efficiently, wide enough to stay balanced through the acceleration.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Base widening through the first steps, costing efficiency and drive; or narrowing so far the receiver crosses over and loses balance.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center along the blocking trajectory, and its rate of change across the approach - controlled acceleration followed by deceleration into contact, not a flat sprint. NOTE: the defender is NOT in frame in a solo clip, so cushion distance cannot be measured; only the receiver's own velocity profile is assessable.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - Blocking - Approach / Closing Velocity
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The receiver closes the cushion under control - accelerating to eat up ground, then gathering before contact rather than running through the block at full speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Over-running the block - arriving at full speed with no gather, so the receiver loses balance on contact and the defender sheds him easily. (Cushion distance needs the defender in frame.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Stride length per step along the release heading, expressed in shoulder widths, EXPANDING progressively from the high-frequency release steps to maximum extension at top speed. Plus lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, which must stay near zero - the seam lane is narrow and drift ruins the concept spacing. Also the rate of rise of the shoulder midpoint out of the low release posture. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading. There is NO break in this route.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Seam - Release
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Low out, then stretch it - stay on your track.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish a strict linear track down the hashes or the seam lane, then transition smoothly into top-end sprint posture with stride lengths opening to maximum expansion, chin tucked and core locked on the track.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Hip, Right Hip, Pelvis Center, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BAILING OFF-TRACK - drifting wide toward the sideline or inside toward the middle right off the snap. Scurrying off the track ruins the spacing of the concept and runs the receiver straight into zone defenders.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands fire up and forward as the plant lands - striking, clearing or bypassing the defender's jam in the same instant the body drives.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The plant knee drops into deep flexion at contact, loading the leg as a high-speed spring that will fire the receiver out on the new line.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector of the plant foot compared against the new route path angle - the two should align. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee (shin) vector - the toe should be pulled UP so the heel contacts first. Check which of Heel or Foot Index reaches its lowest vertical position first at touchdown: heel-first is correct. (3) STEP COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center at contact - the foot should land directly beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead of it. Cross-check horizontal ankle velocity at strike for slide.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Strike - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toe up, heel first - plant under yourself, don't reach.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The outside foot lands with the toe pointing exactly down the new route angle, acting as a steering mechanism rather than just a brake. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which both preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still accelerating vertically until the instant the weight drops.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BLIND PLANT - the toe points straight ahead or wide of the new path, so the foot brakes instead of steering and the receiver slips off the anchor. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early by showing the defender the receiver is gathering rather than still running.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) HEAD ROTATION HELD: head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) maintaining a strict rotational angle back over the shoulder, with the head vector pointing at the wrist midpoint. Any forward yaw back toward the end zone before the wrists close is the PEEKING fault, and it is measured as the frame at which that yaw begins. (2) WRIST CUSHION: wrist angle staying loose, with a small downward give at contact rather than a rigid barrier. NOTE: palm orientation (up to the sky vs forward) is the defining feature here and needs the HAND LANDMARKER; head rotation and sprint continuity are measurable today.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Over the Shoulder - The Strike
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Palms to the sky - don't peek forward.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The eyes track the nose of the ball dropping from the sky straight down into the open palms. The wrists stay completely loose and cushioned right before impact, letting the ball melt into the fingers without disrupting the running stride.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: PEEKING - letting the head drift back forward toward the end zone just before the ball drops into the bucket, so it hits the helmet or falls straight through the hands. THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Ankle-to-ankle horizontal distance compared against shoulder width (L-R Shoulder) as the scale unit - target approximately 1.0x shoulder width. Size-independent. Measurable from a static frame.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Stable, not stuck — wide enough to balance, narrow enough to go.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of the inside shoulder relative to the outside shoulder (shoulder-line tilt angle), plus torso lean of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector toward the inside lane. A pronounced dip is the sell.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The inside shoulder dips hard and the torso leans into the inside lane, committing the upper body to the fake so the defender has to honour it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders staying level through the crossover, so the upper body never sells the inside move and the defender stays square to the outside release.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] LOW-LATERAL NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today, and the hardest case in the catalogue. Track the wrist midpoint rolling UPWARD and sweeping INWARD across the stomach toward Sternum, while simultaneously tracking Nose pitch and yaw. The head must stay locked in the low-lateral quadrant, following the wrists through the entire sweep, with ZERO upfield yaw until wrist-to-Sternum distance reaches near zero. Measured as the angular gap in both axes across every retraction frame, plus the exact frame at which any upfield rotation begins relative to the frame the wrists reach the torso.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Away - Low - The Tuck
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Watch it touch your gut before you look up.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a flat 90 degrees held linear across the field. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory travelling either forward downfield or backward toward the line of scrimmage (curvature in the path). Plus head yaw snapping back over the inside shoulder after the break, and horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; ball location needs ball tracking.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Cross - Finish
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Flat across the field - no bubble.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line across the formation, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Nose, Left Ear, Right Ear
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BUBBLING THE ROUTE - letting the route angle backward toward the line of scrimmage or bubble downfield. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle between the shoulder line and the hip line (rotational separation) during max-effort acceleration strides, tracked across the 5 yards. Excessive or growing separation indicates energy lost to torso rotation rather than forward drive.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Rotational Economy
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The torso stays quiet through the acceleration - shoulders and hips rotate only as much as the stride requires, so energy goes into forward drive rather than twisting.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hip, Right Hip, Sternum, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Excessive torso rotation during max-effort strides - the shoulders counter-rotating hard against the hips, wasting energy that should go into forward drive.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles held at their deep breakdown values across the pause frames - maintained, not extending. The measurement is stability of the angle over the window.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Bait - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The deep knee bend is maintained through the pause, keeping the lower body loaded like a spring ready to fire on the plant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knees extending during the pause, so the stored energy leaks away and the drive out has to be generated from scratch.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating to align parallel with the new exit trajectory, plus the time taken from the plant to reach that alignment. Additionally, path of Pelvis Center across the exit frames fitted against a straight line - the CURVATURE of that path is the rounding measurement.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Finish - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips rotate rapidly to sit parallel with the new exit trajectory, locking the receiver onto a sharp straight line out of the break.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: ROUNDING - the exit trajectory curves rather than forming a sharp line, so the defender recovers the ground the stop had won. Usually caused by the hips rotating too slowly out of the plant.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center and bilateral knee flexion, expressed in torso lengths - the whole frame must lower. CRITICALLY, cross-check the Spine vector angle (Pelvis Center to Sternum) against the hip-to-knee vector to distinguish a knee-and-hip sink from BENDING AT THE WAIST: if the hips stay high while the torso folds forward, that is the fault. Plus wrists dropping low with elbows tucked close to the torso, and PINKY convergence with palms up. NOTE: there is NO pinky landmark in the 33-point pose model - inverted-hand detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER. Body lowering is fully measurable today.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Center - Low - Extend & Bait
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Sink your base - pinkies together, palms up.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Track the downward trajectory and lower the entire body frame by bending at the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist. Drop the arms toward the grass with elbows tucked close to the torso, then invert the hands completely - pinky fingers pressed together, palms facing upward - creating a clean scoop to cradle the dipping ball.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Spine, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: BENDING AT THE WAIST - keeping the legs straight and simply leaning over. This ruins balance, alters eye level dramatically, and prevents running after the catch. THUMBS-UP MISTAKE - trying to catch a low ball with the thumbs together like a chest catch, forcing the hands upside down so the ball slips straight through onto the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held on the inside fake alignment right up to the plant frame, with rotation beginning only at or after that frame. The measurement is the TIMING of the turn relative to the plant's ground contact. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Diamond Cut - Head / Eyes
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The head holds the inside fake alignment right up to the exact plant frame, then prepares to snap back - the deception is maintained to the last possible instant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head starting to turn back outside before the plant lands, giving the defender an early warning and letting them jump the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Amplitude and frequency of wrist displacement across the push step, sustained at the level established on the attack step. A drop in amplitude indicates the receiver is easing off before the cut.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The arm pump continues at full amplitude through the push step, sustaining the impression of a slant or post being run at full effort.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arm pump dropping off during the push step, which signals to the defender that the receiver is about to stop rather than continuing inside.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Displacement of the first moving ankle between the stance frame and its first ground contact, resolved along the release heading in the image plane. Negative displacement indicates a false step. Cross-check Pelvis Center displacement over the same window. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the release heading, not via MediaPipe Z, which is unreliable monocular.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - Stance-to-Step Transition
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the drive begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Hip, Right Hip, Pelvis Center, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the stem begins.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of Pelvis Center across the kickstep, expressed in torso lengths. Target is zero net upward displacement - the hips stay sunk at the height established in the stance.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Hips stay sunk low through the kickstep, holding the loaded height established in the stance with no upward rise.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rising during the kickstep, unloading the legs and costing the elastic energy needed to escape.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Knee flexion angle of the lead/drive leg from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector at push-off. Reference range 110-130 degrees - acute enough to maximise ground force production out of the stance. NOTE: this range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The drive leg holds an acute bend - roughly 110 to 130 degrees - producing maximum ground force to launch onto the diagonal.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Drive leg too straight at push-off, producing little ground force, so the attack step lacks the urgency needed to make the fake believable.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a flat 90 degrees held linear toward the sideline. The fault signal is any component of that trajectory travelling BACK toward the line of scrimmage. Plus head yaw snapping back over the inside shoulder after the break, and horizontal displacement of the outside wrist confirming the arm drive. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; ball location needs ball tracking.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Flat - Finish
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Flat to the boundary - don't drift back.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, sprint flat along the line toward the boundary, snap the eyes back over the inside shoulder to look for the ball, and secure the catch while bracing to turn upfield.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Nose, Left Ear, Right Ear
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to maximise the open void. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak vertical height of the lead knee relative to Pelvis Center (knee drive), expressed in torso lengths, across the first strides of the burst.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Vertical Burst - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The lead knee drives high out of the transition, taking immediate ground upfield and accelerating the receiver toward top speed.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Low knee drive out of the burst, so the first strides are short and shuffling and the receiver takes too long to reach full speed after the transition.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak vertical velocity of the trailing wrist and whether it passes above the shoulder plane (swipe/chop/swim), timed against the burst push-off. The measurement is the velocity and the clearance height, not the hand shape. NOTE: the specific hand action (swipe vs chop vs swim) needs the Hand landmarker; the arm path is measurable from pose.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Kickstep Crossover - Outside Burst - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The trailing arm drives sharply past the shoulder plane - swipe, chop or swim - clearing the defender's hands as the body escapes outside.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Hand, Right Hand
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: No hand action at the escape, or an arm path that never clears the shoulder plane, leaving the defender's hands attached through the release. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles across the breakdown steps, compared against their stem values - both should transition from sprint drive angles into deep flexion, acting as shock absorbers. The measurement is the magnitude and speed of that transition.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Stop - Load - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Both knees move from maximum sprint drive into deep bilateral flexion, working as shock absorbers to soak up the speed the stem built.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knees staying relatively straight through the breakdown, so there is nothing to absorb the momentum - the receiver skids, stumbles, or needs extra steps to stop.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal distance between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - should be minimal, the cleat landing directly beneath the hips. A high separation is the overstriding fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a rigid ankle lock, heel reaching its lowest vertical point before the Foot Index. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector pivoting to a sharp 90 degrees toward the middle of the field relative to the stem heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - In - Power Plant
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Ankle locked, cleat under your hips - don't reach.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The instant the eyes locate the inside lane, drive the outside cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 90-degree angle toward the middle of the field.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut. Also: THE FLOPPY-FOOT SLIDE - planting with a loose, downward-pointing toe out in front of the chest, lacking the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Wrist height relative to Sternum and Pelvis Center (waist-to-chest band); horizontal separation between the wrists (uncrossed, independent); elbow angle for relaxed vs rigid. Hand OPENNESS and finger detail need the Hand landmarker - not available from the 33-point pose model.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Standard - Stance - Hand Position
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Hands loose and free - ready to fight hands.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Hands remain relaxed, uncrossed, and independent. Hands are positioned near the waist or slightly higher in front of the chest depending on anticipated coverage. Hands remain free to immediately react to a press defender.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Hand, Right Hand, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands crossed over the body's midline, clamped tight to the torso, or held so low or high that the receiver cannot react to a press. Arms rigid rather than relaxed. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Onset and rate of yaw rotation of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) toward the break direction. The rotation should BEGIN in this phase but remain partial - the full snap happens at the plant. Measured as angular displacement and its timing relative to the head turn.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Bait - Hips
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips begin to uncoil toward the break direction, starting the rotation that the plant will complete.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rotating fully before the plant, committing early and letting the defender break on the route; or not uncoiling at all, so the plant has to do all the work and the cut rounds off.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Shoulder-line angle (L-R Shoulder vector) rotating to square with the 45 degree diagonal, plus torso drive angle of the Pelvis-Center-to-Sternum vector relative to vertical, which should stay low and forward. NOTE: resolved as image-plane angles, not via MediaPipe Z.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Diamond Release - The Attack Step - Shoulders
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The shoulders rotate fully square to the 45 degree line with the torso driving low and forward, exactly as they would on a genuine slant.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum, Pelvis Center, Spine
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Shoulders lagging behind the feet or staying upright rather than driving low onto the diagonal, so the upper body never commits to the lie.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step's ankle displacement relative to the intended release heading, measured in the image plane. Lateral drift is the deviation from that heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - First Steps - 5 Yards - First Step Direction
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the stem develops.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Distance from each wrist to Sternum, expressed in torso lengths - the wrists should retract close to the lower ribcage into a compact ready position. Plus elbow flexion angle for a tucked rather than extended arm.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Slide Step Release - The Hesitation - Hands
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hands retract tight to the lower ribcage into a compact ready position, loaded to strike as soon as contact comes.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Sternum
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hands hanging loose or away from the frame during the pause, giving the defender something to grab and leaving nothing loaded for the strike. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the release heading - target is a strict 45 degrees held linear. The fault signal is that angle opening toward 90 degrees (flattening across). Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline confirming the cross-body punch, and forward velocity sustained through the break rather than dropping. NOTE: resolved in the image plane; catching the ball in stride needs ball tracking.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame. (1) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector of the plant foot compared against the angle of the new route path - the two should align. A plant foot still pointing along the old stem heading is the fault signal, and shows up as lateral ankle slide after contact. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee (shin) vector - the toe should be pulled UP so the heel contacts first. Check which of Heel or Foot Index reaches its lowest vertical position first at touchdown: heel-first is correct. (3) STEP COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center at contact - the foot should land directly beneath the centre of mass, not reaching ahead of it. Cross-check horizontal ankle velocity at strike for slide.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Cuts - Speed - Strike - Footwork
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toe up, heel first - plant under yourself, don't reach.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The outside cutting foot lands with the toe already pointed along the new route path, steering the body into the break rather than braking against it. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion so the heel bites the grass first, giving clean, firm contact instead of a slide or a stubbed toe. The step stays compact and lands directly beneath the centre of mass - no over-extending or lunging - which preserves body control and keeps the defender believing the receiver is still running vertically until the instant the weight drops.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE BLIND PLANT - the foot lands still pointing straight downfield instead of along the new path, so the receiver slides outward, loses his base, and the cut becomes a skid rather than a redirect. Toe left down (plantarflexed) rather than pulled up, so the receiver slides through the plant or stubs the toe instead of biting the ground heel-first. Over-extending or lunging the plant step out ahead of the centre of mass, which costs body control and tips the break early.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical height of the shoulder midpoint expressed in torso lengths, and the SLOPE of its rise across the 5 yards. A smooth, gradual, near-linear rise is correct; a step-change (popping upright) is the fault.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise smoothly and gradually across the 5 yards as speed builds, reaching upright running posture only once the acceleration phase is complete.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Popping upright prematurely rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and cutting acceleration short.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak lateral acceleration of Pelvis Center toward the inside lane, resolved in the image plane, plus rotation of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) toward that lane. Both should spike together to sell the inside move.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips drive hard laterally across the defender's face, rotating toward the inside lane so the whole body sells the fake rather than just the feet.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips staying square while only the feet cross over - the fake is not sold, and the defender reads the outside release immediately.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Drive-leg knee extension angle at push-off, approaching full extension (near 180 degrees), measured from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vector. Simultaneously the lead knee should FLEX to gain ground. The measurement is the opposing pair - full extension behind, flexion in front.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Press Release - Split Release - The Plant & Drive - Knees
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The drive leg extends fully to deliver every bit of force, while the lead knee flexes and drives forward to take immediate ground into the lane.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Drive leg failing to extend fully, leaving force in the ground; or the lead knee not driving through, so the first stride out of the plant is short.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Displacement of Pelvis Center after the plant, resolved along the stem heading in the image plane - it must travel BACK toward the line of scrimmage. Near-zero displacement (standing still) is the fault signal. Plus the shoulder line squaring fully to the quarterback, and horizontal distance of both wrists from Sternum increasing at the catch point (hands extended away from the frame). NOTE: resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z. Whether the receiver shortened the throw or shielded a defender needs the ball and defender in frame.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Curl - Finish
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Come back to the ball - never wait on it.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, open the chest completely to the quarterback, work back downhill toward the ball to shorten the distance of the throw, and secure the catch with the hands extended away from the frame.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angular velocity of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) rotating from the inside fake toward the outside vertical lane, plus the change in Pelvis Center trajectory heading from lateral to upfield. cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The hips rotate sharply from the inside fake toward the sideline and upfield, converting the lateral momentum of the crossover into vertical drive up the field.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Hips rotating slowly or incompletely, so the receiver drifts sideways out of the release instead of driving upfield, losing ground on the route stem.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Vertical drop of Pelvis Center and bilateral knee flexion, expressed in torso lengths. CRITICALLY, cross-check the Spine vector against the hip-to-knee vector AND the shoulder-line tilt to distinguish a knee-and-hip sink from WAIST-BENDING SIDEWAYS: hips staying high while the torso folds laterally is the fault. Plus wrists dropping BOTH downward and laterally (diagonal drop toward the grass on the catch side), elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, and PINKY convergence with palms up and out. NOTE: no pinky landmark exists in the 33-point pose model - inverted-hand detection needs the HAND LANDMARKER.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Pelvis Center, Left Hip, Right Hip, Left Knee, Right Knee, Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Spine, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Distance between successive foot-strikes expressed in shoulder widths (L-R Shoulder as the scale unit). Stride length must EXPAND progressively from Step 1 through Steps 4-5 - the measurement is the progression, not any single stride.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held at zero relative to the stem heading, measured as low angular variance across the stem frames. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Bilateral knee flexion angles from the Hip-Knee-Ankle vectors. Reference range 90-110 degrees into an athletic squat. Plus horizontal position of Pelvis Center relative to the Foot Index pair, confirming weight balanced over the balls of the feet. NOTE: the 90-110 range is an uncalibrated starting reference, not a rule.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Knees staying too straight to load the split, or weight settling back onto the heels so the receiver cannot push off cleanly.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a strict 45 degrees toward the corner, held linear. cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Distance from each wrist to Sternum, expressed in torso lengths - the wrists should retract close to the lower Sternum/ribcage into a compact ready position. Plus elbow flexion angle for a tucked vs extended arm.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THREE signals at the plant frame, on the OUTSIDE foot. (1) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the plant ankle relative to Pelvis Center - the cleat must land firmly beneath the body weight, not reaching ahead. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - the toe pulled up before the foot strikes, grounding the receiver cleanly. The toe is pulled up before the foot strikes to ground cleanly. Instantly point the toe and direct the final step down a flat 90-degree track across the field, masking the horizontal break until the last possible instant.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) held at zero relative to the stem heading, measured as low angular variance across the stem frames. NOTE: orientation only - actual EYE GAZE is not measurable from the 33-point pose model.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Forward velocity of Pelvis Center along the stem heading, held constant at top speed, plus vertical oscillation of Pelvis Center measured as variance in torso lengths - minimal bounce indicates efficient top-end running.

Track the wrist midpoint retracting on a diagonal (downward AND inward across the chest) toward Sternum, and simultaneously track BOTH Nose pitch and yaw. The head must follow that same diagonal path - measured as correlation between head direction and wrist position in both axes across the retraction frames, plus frame offset. This is the most demanding tracking case in the catalogue: the head must rotate on two axes at once while the body is landing. Plus knee flexion increasing on landing.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) rotating inside across the middle, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the third stride's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. NOTE: orientation only - whether the receiver actually READ the inside linebackers or picked up the release cannot be confirmed from a solo clip.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Eyes inside at the top of step three.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: At the exact peak of the third stride, snap the head and eyes inside across the middle of the field first. The visual snap instantly clears vision to read the inside linebackers and pick up the ball's release.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Eye, Right Eye, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder, Left Ankle, Right Ankle
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks across the defender's face without having cleared his vision - and on a route this quick, the ball is often already out. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal position of the outside wrist relative to Sternum at the plant - it should cross the body's midline to shield the chest. Plus elbow flexion angle confirming a tucked protective position rather than an extended arm.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The outside hand crosses over the chest frame at the plant, shielding the body against any late contact from a defender closing on the fake.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] TWO signals at the impact frame. (1) TRACKING: Nose pitched UPWARD (Nose relative to the ear midpoint), with the head vector pointing at the midpoint between the elevated wrists - the receiver is looking through the thumb window. Head pitching back down toward the turf before the wrists close is THE BLIND PULL fault. (2) APEX: vertical height of the wrist midpoint should reach its maximum at or immediately before the impact frame, not after - a peak occurring late means the receiver caught it on the way down rather than at the top. NOTE: fingertip wrap and the ball itself need the Hand landmarker and object detection.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: THE BLIND PULL - tilting the head back down toward the turf before the hands secure the ball, resulting in a blind, clapping attempt at the apex. cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] THE NOSE-TO-THE-TUCK METRIC - fully measurable from pose today, no Hand landmarker required. Track the vertical descent of the wrist midpoint as it retracts toward Sternum, and simultaneously track Nose pitch (Nose relative to the ear midpoint). The head must pitch DOWNWARD in step with the descending wrists - measured as the correlation between the two across the retraction frames, plus any frame offset between them. A Nose vector that stops following the wrists, or yaws away upfield, before the wrists reach Sternum is the fault. Plus wrist-to-Sternum distance closing to near zero (the tuck) and elbow wrapping over.

(1) COMPACTNESS: displacement between the plant ankle and Pelvis Center - the cleat must land directly beneath the hips, not overextended. High separation is the overstriding fault. (2) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector - toe pulled UP into a firm ankle lock before impact. (3) TOE DIRECTION: Heel-to-Foot-Index vector directing to a sharp 45 degrees inward relative to the release heading.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Routes - Tree - Slant - Angle Plant
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toe up, under your hips - slice across his face.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldP92I0CdHLKpj7d: The split-second the eyes turn, drive the outside foot down into a controlled step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion before impact to establish a firm ankle lock, and the step is not overextended. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly directing the toe at a sharp 45 degrees toward the middle to slice across the defender's face without losing linear body control.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Head yaw held at zero relative to the stem heading across the breakdown frames, with rotation beginning only at the visual snap. The measurement is the TIMING of the first head movement relative to the chop steps. NOTE: orientation only - gaze is not pose-measurable.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Contact time of the plant foot from strike to toe-off (shorter is better), plus the height and length of the first step out along the new heading - it should be low and linear rather than high or rounded. cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: A gather step between the plant and the drive out, or a high, short first step - either way the stored energy is wasted and the defender recovers the separation the stop created.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Applied to EVERY stride rather than a single plant. (1) DORSIFLEXION: angle between the Foot-Index-to-Heel vector and the Ankle-to-Knee shin vector at each ground contact - the toe pulled up into a rigid ankle lock. A Foot Index pointing downward at impact is the fault signal. (2) COMPACTNESS: horizontal position of the landing ankle relative to Pelvis Center at each strike - landing beneath the centre of mass, not extending beyond it. (3) LINEARITY: lateral deviation of the ankle path and Pelvis Center from the release heading, held near zero to stay in the void. (4) Head yaw rotating to track over the INSIDE shoulder while the Pelvis Center path stays linear.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Toes up, straight down the lane - look over the inside shoulder.

Steps stay compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding, toes pulling up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride for a rigid ankle lock, while the eyes track the ball over the inside shoulder.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Left Knee, Right Knee, Pelvis Center, Nose, Left Ear, Right Ear
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to outrun a deep safety, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability and caps top-end speed. Also: drifting laterally out of the void.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Step frequency across the final two steps before contact, plus the ratio of ground contact time to flight time. Short choppy steps show as high frequency and a high contact-time ratio - the feet stay near the ground rather than striding out.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Arriving on long strides rather than chopping the feet down, leaving the receiver committed and unable to adjust when the defender moves.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Lead knee staying stiff through the load step, so the sink cannot be absorbed and the receiver either pops up or loses balance going into the plant.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Path of Pelvis Center across the frames after the plant, fitted against a straight line along the new route heading. cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: ROUNDING THE ANGLE - the pelvis trajectory forms a wide curve instead of a sharp linear exit, giving the defender time and space to recover the separation the cut had created.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Peak angular velocity of head yaw (Nose vector relative to the ear midpoint) toward the sideline, and critically the FRAME at which that rotation begins compared against the plant foot's ground-contact frame - the head must lead the plant. cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the Pelvis Center exit trajectory relative to the stem heading - target is a flat 90 degrees, aligned immediately after the plant rather than settling over several strides. Plus horizontal displacement of the outside wrist across the Sternum midline, confirming the cross-body punch. NOTE: resolved in the image plane against the stem heading.

Measured as the angular gap between head direction and wrist midpoint in both axes. Plus wrist height held below the hip line, and the wrist pair positioned UNDER the ball's incoming path rather than beside it. NOTE: fingertip angle and the curl need the Hand landmarker; the ball needs object detection.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Final angle of the hip line (L-R Hip vector) at and immediately after the plant, compared against the head yaw angle and the plant foot's toe direction - all three should converge on the same new heading. Divergence between them is the fault signal.

Track the lateral retraction of the wrist midpoint sweeping back across the torso toward Sternum, and simultaneously track head YAW. The head must sweep inward MATCHING THE SPEED of the returning wrists - measured as the correlation between the two curves plus any frame offset. The specific risk here is that the rotational momentum of the sweep rips the eyes off the ball, so any yaw that outruns or lags the wrists is the fault. Plus wrist-to-Sternum distance closing to near zero.
cellValuesByFieldId.fldCHVDdJCO7Jl2Td: WR - Catching - Away - Chest/Mid - The Tuck
cellValuesByFieldId.fldMVEbUCKt7CF8LT: Sweep it in and let your chin ride with it.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Nose, Left Ear, Right Ear, Neck, Left Wrist, Right Wrist, Left Elbow, Right Elbow, Sternum, Left Shoulder, Right Shoulder
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Angle of the first step out of the plant relative to the incoming 45 degree diagonal - a sharp direction reversal forming the diamond path. Plus peak acceleration of Pelvis Center along the new outside heading, and the contact time of the push-off. Resolved in the image plane, not via MediaPipe Z.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldW2zGQGNOjFxg4l: Left Ankle, Right Ankle, Left Foot Index, Right Foot Index, Left Heel, Right Heel, Pelvis Center
cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: A rounded or gradual change of direction rather than a sharp reversal, so the diamond flattens into a curve and the defender recovers the ground the fake bought.

cellValuesByFieldId.fld9xx1Oppv32GP5d: [DRAFT] Horizontal extension distance of both wrists away from Sternum at the catch approach, expressed in torso lengths - maximum reach, with the wrists clearly forward of the chest plane rather than resting against it. Plus elbow flexion angle (relaxed, not locked). Plus convergence of the thumbs and index fingers into a diamond. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.

cellValuesByFieldId.fldbS3BRiNwYEP3pG: Low knee drive out of the break, so the receiver shuffles back up to speed and the window the cut opened closes before the ball arrives.
